summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted with fever and chills two days after his chemotherapy infusion. Workup revealed elevated bilirubin and transaminitis, concerning for biliary obstruction and cholangitis. A CT scan showed persistent dilation of the right hepatic duct with functioning stents. He underwent ERCP, which confirmed sludge and stones in the right biliary stent, which were cleared. He was treated with IV antibiotics, transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin and metronidazole, and showed clinical improvement with normalization of liver function tests and resolution of fever. His hyponatremia resolved with hydration, and cytopenias were attributed to recent chemotherapy. He was discharged home on a 14-day antibiotic course with follow-up planned with oncology.
problems: Malignant neoplasm of intrahepatic bile ducts
Fever presenting with conditions classified elsewhere
Nonspecific elevation of levels of transaminase or lactic acid dehydrogenase [LDH]
Hypertrophy (benign) of prostate without urinary obstruction and other lower urinary tract symptom (LUTS)
